rule_en: Secondary ('orbital revolution') progression: the measure of time is one day. Planetary changes on the nth day after birth symbolise the events of the nth year of life.
quote: The measure of time in this system is one day. That is to say, the changes among the heavenly bodies during the first day of life symbolise the events that will occur during the first year of life
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section A, Ch. VI 'The Progression of the Horoscope', II 'Progression by Orbital Revolution', p.27
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; wording confirmed against the independent OCR of the 1936 DLI edition (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.128064), which has the same sentence. [verify: OCR text match 0.96; found on PDF p.39]

rule_en: Progressed horoscope for age N = chart cast for N complete days after birth (same birth time).
quote: A map for ten complete days after birth will form a Progressed Horoscope for ten years of age.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. VI, p.27
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.39]

rule_en: Each day after birth = one year of life; in that time the progressed MC advances about one degree. The Ascendant also advances, but at a rate that depends on the table of houses.
quote: Each day after birth represents one whole year of life. During that time, the M.C. (as the midheaven is called) has progressed about one degree.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. V 'The Author's System', 'The Progressive Angles', p.25
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('wliole' read as 'whole'). [verify: OCR text match 0.99; found on PDF p.37]

rule_en: The progressed Sun and MC both advance roughly one degree per year. The progressed Ascendant's rate depends on whether a sign of long or short ascension is rising.
quote: the mid-heaven and the Sun both advance, roughly speaking, about one degree per annum ; the rate of advance of the ascendant depends upon whether a sign of long or short ascension is rising.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. VI, p.30
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.42]

rule_en: When a new sign reaches the progressed Ascendant, its ruler gains influence over the temperament, but the natal ruler stays paramount for life.
quote: the horoscope progresses, at the rate of about one degree per year, until in course of time a new sign comes to the ascendant
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section B, Ch. IX 'The Progressed Ascendant', p.49
notes: Same paragraph: 'though the influence of the original ruler of the nativity remains paramount throughout life'. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.61]

rule_en: The progressed Sun's aspects are like the hour hand: they mark the period when 'directions' are due. The Moon is the minute hand that times when they operate.
quote: The Sun is as it were the 'short hand' of a clock marking the hour, the time when the "directions" are due. The Moon is the 'long hand' pointing to the minute
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section B, Ch. X 'Solar Aspects', p.68
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('Jwnr' read as 'hour', 'short hand 'of' spacing). [verify: OCR text match 0.97; found on PDF p.80]

rule_en: Duration (effective orb) of a progressed solar aspect: at least three years, about one year applying, one year exact and one year separating. Since the progressed Sun moves about 1° a year, this is roughly a 1° orb on either side. Leo states it in years, not degrees.
quote: Solar aspects operate during a period of three years or more. One year when the solar aspect is becoming complete, a year when complete, and another year as the influence passes off.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. X 'Solar Aspects', p.68
notes: No explicit 'orb of 1 degree' sentence was found in Leo's own Sections A-C of the 1906 book. The 1° reading is my inference from the 1°/year rate. The 1936 revised edition adds a lunar orb of about a month (not used: posthumous revision). [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.80]

rule_en: Solar aspects are taken from the progressed Sun to the radical (natal) planet. Aspects to progressed planets may also be read, but in terms of the progressed horoscope rather than the nativity.
quote: The whole of the ensuing Solar aspects are considered as being formed between the progressed position of the Sun and the radical position of the planet in question.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. X, 'Important Preliminary Notes', N.B., p.69
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; the 1906 OCR is damaged at 'radical position' (reads 'radical ptnHmt'); the reading 'position' is inferred from context and the worked example that follows (progressed Sun reaching natal Jupiter's degree). Verify against the page image before display. [verify: OCR text match 0.95; found on PDF p.81]

rule_en: Progressed Moon: moves 12-13 degrees in a year (one day). List each degree it passes; each successive degree comes due about one month later.
quote: since the Moon moves in a year (day) twelve or thirteen degrees, it is advisable to set out each degree passed through during that time
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. VII 'An Example of the Calculation of a Progressed Horoscope', p.41
notes: Same passage: 'each after the first will be due about a month later' (OCR: 'bXL due ahoat'). [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.53]

rule_en: Progressed Moon passes through one sign in about 2.5 years and round the whole zodiac in about 28 years.
quote: For the Moon by progressive motion moves through one sign of the zodiac in two years and a half
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section C, Ch. XIII 'Transits', 'The General Effect of Transits', p.202
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('progresave' read as 'progressive', 'xodiac' as 'zodiac'). Same page: 'the progressed Moon takes twenty-eight and Saturn thirty years to complete the circle'. [verify: OCR text match 0.96; found on PDF p.214]

rule_en: Progressed lunar aspects are only of vital significance when they match in nature the solar and mutual aspects then operating. Otherwise they only show what may happen. The Moon brings the major aspect to fruition.
quote: The Moon's aspects, formed by the progress of the Moon round the horoscope, are only of vital significance when they coincide in nature with the Solar and Mutual aspects.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section B, Ch. XI 'Lunar Positions and Aspects', 'Important Note regarding the Moon's Aspects', p.95
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('signincaace' read as 'significance'). [verify: OCR text match 0.98; found on PDF p.107]

rule_en: Progressed Moon to radical planets: read in terms of the natal chart (radix). Progressed Moon to progressed planets: read in terms of the progressed horoscope (its house rulerships).
quote: the Moon's aspects to radical planets are to be interpreted in terms of the Radix, while those to the progressed planets are to be rendered in terms of the Progressed Horoscope
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XI, p.94
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('radicMl' read as 'radical', 'inter pretedjn' spacing, 'fngnati' as 'progressed'). Wording confirmed against the 1936 DLI OCR. [verify: OCR text match 0.90; found on PDF p.106]

rule_en: Progressed Moon through houses: its passage through each house of the radix or the progressed chart shows the kind of events most likely. E.g. through the 1st house it brings the personality to the fore, breaks up existing conditions, and crossing the Ascendant nearly always brings changes.
quote: will bring all matters connected with the personality to the fore, and much will depend upon the native's own actions and upon his own attitude of mind
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XI, 'A. The Lunar Position: (a) as regards the Houses', I., p.96
notes: Sentence subject garbled in OCR ('The Moon passing through the First House of the nativity or the progressed horoscope'). Houses I-XII run pp.96-100. Leo notes the effect depends on how prominent the corresponding sign is in the nativity. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.108]

rule_en: Progressed Moon through signs: the contents point the reader to the Moon-in-signs table on p.23, which describes how the Moon's sign tinges the feelings.
quote: The Moon in the signs of the zodiac will tinge the soul or personality according to the nature of the sign it is in
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. V, 'The Moon and her Influence in "Directions"', p.23
notes: The p.23-24 table is badly OCR'd and is not extracted here. The contents line 'Lunar Position … (b) as regards the Signs (vide p.23)' is also damaged in OCR. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.35]

rule_en: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune move too slowly to form new progressed aspects to natal planets that were not already within orbs at birth. Leo gives no delineations for them.
quote: are so slow in their motion that by progression they can seldom or never form any aspects to planets in the radical horoscope that were not "within orbs" at birth.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section B, Ch. XII 'Mutual Aspects', end, p.189
notes: Subject of the sentence: 'The remaining planets, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune,'. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.201]

rule_en: A year with no progressed solar aspect is less eventful, whatever other influences show.
quote: When there are no Solar aspects operating, during the period for which the calculations concerning "directions" have been made, the year that lies ahead is not likely to be so important or eventful
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. X 'Important Preliminary Notes', p.69
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('bavs' read as 'have'). [verify: OCR text match 0.99; found on PDF p.81]

rule_en: Hierarchy: transits are subordinate to the directions (progressions) in force, and directions are always inferior to the radical (natal) chart.
quote: all "transits" are subsidiary in their effects to the "directions" operating at the time, just as the latter are in all cases inferior in power to the "radical" influences
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section B, 'Concluding Note to this Section', p.192
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('&et', 'fal all cases' and quote-mark noise cleaned). [verify: OCR text match 0.97; found on PDF p.204]

rule_en: Main transiting planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Mars and Uranus crossing the sensitive points of the nativity. Saturn contracts, Jupiter expands, Mars quickens, Uranus hastens or precipitates.
quote: approximately known by giving a little attention to the " transits " of the superior planets, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars and Uranus; i.e., the dates on which these planets cross the various sensitive points in the nativity.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Section C, Ch. XIII 'Transits', p.193
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('transtis' read as 'transits'). [verify: OCR text match 0.99; found on PDF p.205]

rule_en: Forecasts from transits that ignore the current directions in the progressed horoscope are vague and general. Transits supplement and help define the events shown by directions.
quote: Any prognostications based upon " transits " without having regard to the current directions then in force (as shown in the progressed horoscope) can necessarily be only vague and general
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XIII, p.193
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.205]

rule_en: Venus and Mercury have very slight influence as transiting planets, except when one of them is the ruling planet.
quote: Venus and Mercury have very slight influence as transiting planets and are rarely, if ever, noticed.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XIII, p.201
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.213]

rule_en: Transits only activate natal influences. An adverse transit accentuates an evil direction then operating. Saturn transiting the progressed Moon brings out the evil of a lunar square or opposition to Saturn; Jupiter transiting it doubles a benefic lunar aspect to Jupiter.
quote: It may be taken as a safe rule that when an evil direction is operating an adverse transit will accentuate it.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XIII 'The General Effect of Transits', p.202
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.214]

rule_en: One of the most certain transits: Saturn over the progressed Moon's place ('hunting the Moon'). It can last many years because both move about one sign per 2.5 years.
quote: One of the most certain and direct transits is that of Saturn "hunting the Moon," as it is termed, that is, when Saturn is in transit over the Moon's progressed place.
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XIII, p.202
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('tranats', 'liunt- ing the Mood' cleaned). [verify: OCR text match 0.97; found on PDF p.214]

rule_en: Transits have most effect when several planets are grouped in one sign, especially a satellitium in an angle. Note the declinations of transiting planets.
quote: The declinations of the transiting planets should always be carefully noted
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. XIII, p.203
notes: [verify: OCR text match 0.97; found on PDF p.215]

rule_en: Moon in Scorpio (Leo, hedged keywords): firm, determined, self-reliant, obstinate; can be irritable.
quote: and assured, and well able to stand alone and fight his own battles.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres', 'The Influence of the Moon in the Twelve Signs', p.83
notes: Leo treats the Moon as the Personality. Nearly the same wording is in Astrology for All (1910) Ch. XVII pp.64-70. Printed pp.63-64 (start of that chapter) are missing from the DLI scan. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.107]

rule_en: Moon in Sagittarius (Leo, hedged keywords): quick, restless, active, fond of travel; religious, intuitive.
quote: This gives a quick, restless and unsettled manner, either to the body or mind
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres', 'The Influence of the Moon in the Twelve Signs', p.83
notes: Leo treats the Moon as the Personality. Nearly the same wording is in Astrology for All (1910) Ch. XVII pp.64-70. Printed pp.63-64 (start of that chapter) are missing from the DLI scan. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.107]

rule_en: Moon in Capricorn (Leo, hedged keywords): brings before the public, popularity or notoriety with drawbacks; administrative ability.
quote: This tends to bring the native before the public for good or evil, popularity or notoriety, though it usually has some drawback attaching to it
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres', 'The Influence of the Moon in the Twelve Signs', p.84
notes: Leo treats the Moon as the Personality. Nearly the same wording is in Astrology for All (1910) Ch. XVII pp.64-70. Printed pp.63-64 (start of that chapter) are missing from the DLI scan. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.108]

rule_en: Moon in Aquarius (Leo, hedged keywords): unusual, original subjects; humanitarian, joins societies.
quote: Subjects that are unusual, original, eccentric, and novel, attract the native.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres', 'The Influence of the Moon in the Twelve Signs', p.85
notes: Leo treats the Moon as the Personality. Nearly the same wording is in Astrology for All (1910) Ch. XVII pp.64-70. Printed pp.63-64 (start of that chapter) are missing from the DLI scan. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.109]

rule_en: Moon in Pisces (Leo, hedged keywords): quiet, retiring, restless, irresolute, easily discouraged; emotional, psychic.
quote: The native is quiet, retiring, and easy going, is restless and fond of variety, easily changes his mind
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres', 'The Influence of the Moon in the Twelve Signs', p.85
notes: Leo treats the Moon as the Personality. Nearly the same wording is in Astrology for All (1910) Ch. XVII pp.64-70. Printed pp.63-64 (start of that chapter) are missing from the DLI scan. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.109]

rule_en: Uranus (Leo): governs the original, eccentric and unconventional. Strongest for independent 'advanced thinkers'; little effect on those bound by custom.
quote: It appears to govern all things that are original, eccentric, and free to act apart from any conventional groove or accepted custom.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. III 'The Luminaries and the Planets', p.36
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.60]

rule_en: Uranus brings sudden and unexpected events. No precise rules can be given for it.
quote: Sudden and unexpected events will occur, and act in an almost unknowable manner
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. III, p.37
notes: Same page: 'No definite or precise rules can be laid down with regard to Uranus'. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.61]

rule_en: Uranus has less influence on the average person today than any planet except Neptune.
quote: The planet Uranus has less influence at the present day than any other planet except Neptune.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. III, p.36
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.60]

rule_en: Uranus is equally strong in will (action), feeling and thought, hence its sudden effects. When strong it divides life into distinct 'chapters'. Its people are not vacillating but intensely in earnest.
quote: Uranus is remarkable for being equally strong in all three. This accounts to a large extent for the sudden and unexpected nature of the events it brings about
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XI 'Uranus, the Awakener', p.95
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.123]

rule_en: Neptune (Leo): on the whole a faint influence. Linked to uncontrolled mediumship and weak will, but also to the highly advanced psychic. An afflicted Neptune is as a rule undesirable. Leo says more data is needed.
quote: the last discovered planet, has, on the whole, but a faint influence upon our earth and its inhabitants.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. III, p.37
notes: Same page: 'Experience tends to prove that the influence of an afflicted Neptune as a rule is undesirable.' [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.61]

rule_en: Neptune acts mainly on the psychic/emotional plane and little on physical action. It is not evil in itself.
quote: its sphere of influence being largely confined to the psychic or emotional plane.
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XII 'Neptune, the Mystic', p.104
notes: Leo's chapter says it is 'notes by several close students' and that its statements 'must, however, be read as opinions and not as definite knowledge' (p.103). It is not Leo's own doctrine alone. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.132]

rule_en: Uranus and Neptune are 'higher octaves', less in evidence in the ordinary person. Uranus rules inner sight (clairvoyance) and Neptune inner touch (psychometry).
quote: Uranus governs the inner sight (clairvoyance), and Neptune, inner touch (psychometry).
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. III, p.30
notes: OCR spells 'NeEptuneE'; normalised. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.54]

rule_en: In progressions, Uranus and Neptune affect the Moon only slightly for the average person, except when either severely afflicts it (calamity, disagreements, losses).
quote: as the average man is only slightly affected by these two planets, little must be expected from them in most cases, except in the case of severe affliction by either
locator: Alan Leo, The Progressed Horoscope (London: L.N. Fowler / Modern Astrology Office, 1906), Ch. V, 'The Moon and her Influence in "Directions"', p.23
notes: OCR text of the 1906 Google scan normalised for obvious OCR errors; ('aflected bj', 'planeta', 'firom', 'casss' cleaned). [verify: OCR text match 0.97; found on PDF p.35]

rule_en: A horoscope consists of four factors in order of importance: (1) the solar position, (2) the lunar position, (3) the Ascendant, (4) the planetary aspects. The solar position is paramount.
quote: The importance of these four factors is indicated by their order, the solar position being paramount.
locator: Alan Leo, Astrology for All (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1910 edition, Digital Library of India scan), Ch. XVIII 'The Soli-Lunar Combinations or Polarities', 'Preliminary Notes', p.72
notes: The OCR jumbles the numbered list ('(i) The Solar position. The Ascendant. (2) The Lunar position. (4) The Planetary aspects'). The order Sun, Moon, Ascendant, aspects follows from the numbering (3 = Ascendant). [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.83]

rule_en: Sun = life side (Individuality); Moon = form side (Personality and physical characteristics). Blend the two (the 144 Sun-Moon 'polarities').
quote: the Sun represents the life side, governing the Individual, and the Moon the form side, governing the whole of the Personal (and physical) characteristics.
locator: Alan Leo, Astrology for All (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1910 edition, Digital Library of India scan), Ch. XVIII, p.72
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.83]

rule_en: Three centres, the first: the Sun by sign = Individuality (soul, will, authority, vitality); corresponds to the fixed signs.
quote: It represents the Indi- viduality, or the soul of the man, divested of all outer ephemeral phases and moods.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V 'The Three Centres: Sun, Moon, and Ascendant', p.68
notes: Line-break hyphen 'Indi- viduality' as in source. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.92]

rule_en: Second centre: the Moon, judged by sign and by its distance (phase) from the Sun = Personality (feelings, senses); corresponds to the mutable signs.
quote: The second of the three centres is THE Moon, which has to be judged partly by the sign in which it is placed and partly by its distance from the Sun.
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V, p.69
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.93]

rule_en: Third centre: the Ascendant gathers up the twelve houses = the body, brain and inherited disposition; corresponds to the cardinal signs. As the person develops it blends with the Moon, then the Sun, and especially strongly if a luminary is rising.
quote: It gathers up the influences of the twelve mundane houses into one, and stands for the body in general and for the head and brain in particular
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. V, p.70
notes: p.71: 'may become blended first with that of the Moon and afterwards with that of the Sun'. Leo's tabulation: Sun = Individuality, Moon = Personality, Houses/Ascendant = Body. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.94]

rule_en: Ruling planet = lord of the ascending sign, or the strongest or most prominent planet. Angular planets come first (1st house most, 4th least). A rising planet is part ruler. Planets near the 10th/7th cusps or closely aspecting the Ascendant degree count. The planet in closest aspect to the Sun is always important. When in doubt, use the lord of the Ascendant.
quote: in every case where there is the least doubt, the lord of the ascending sign should be considered as the RULING PLANET, for that planet will be the native's representative through life
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. VII 'The Ruling Planet', p.129
notes: Opening definition, same page: "The 'ruling planet' is either the lord of the ascending sign, or else that planet which is strongest or most prominent in the horoscope." [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.153]

rule_en: Synthesis starts from the rising sign. Every position modifies every other and all are centred on the Ascendant. The Sun, Moon or ruling planet can act as further centres.
quote: Every position modifies every other to a greater or less extent, and all are more or less centralised in the ascendant.
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI 'Methods of Synthesis', p.155
notes: p.154 states the Ascendant is 'the starting point of every synthesis' (OCR damaged there). [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.183]

rule_en: Method I: count planets by triplicity (fire/earth/air/water) and quadruplicity (cardinal/fixed/mutable). The dominant pair (e.g. Cardinal-Earth) gives the type, which is then combined with the Ascendant. Break ties using the luminaries and the Ascendant.
quote: The number of planets in signs of fire, earth, air, and water will show which of the triplicities is strongest
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI, I 'The Triplicities and Quadruplicities', p.155
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.183]

rule_en: Method II: classify the Sun, Moon and Ascendant by quadruplicity. All three the same = emphasised 'Will' (cardinal = rapid, fixed = enduring, mutable = 'wise'). Two the same = the stronger prevails, tempered by the weaker (six classes described). All different = come strongly under the rising sign and ruling planet.
quote: the stronger influence prevails, tempered and modified by the weaker.
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI, II 'Sun, Moon and Ascendant', p.157
notes: OCR reads 'modified b3^ the weaker' ('by'). p.160: 'Those who belong to it come strongly under the influence of the rising sign and the ruling planet.' [verify: OCR text match 0.98; found on PDF p.185]

rule_en: Method III: positive vs negative temperament from (1) which luminary is stronger (zodiacal dignity, angularity/elevation), (2) male planets (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus) vs female planets (Venus, Neptune), with Mercury variable, and (3) the majority of planets in odd vs even signs.
quote: The Sun, male planets, and odd signs give the positive temperament, of which man is the type.
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI, III 'Positive and Negative Temperaments', p.161
notes: OCR: 'The_Sun'. [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.189]

rule_en: Method IV: distinguish the ruler of the horoscope (strongest planet) from the lord of the rising sign. The lord of the Ascendant is ruler when dignified, angular (1st/10th/7th), in 9th/11th, or elevated. A strong other planet may rule if the Ascendant lord is in fall or detriment. Never overlook the Ascendant's lord.
quote: In any case the ruler of the rising sign must not be overlooked when delineating a horoscope
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI, IV 'The Ruling Planet', p.164
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.192]

rule_en: Method V: majority sign positions. Four or more planets in the signs of one ruler (e.g. Aries+Scorpio for Mars) strengthen that planet's influence regardless of where the planet itself is. Scattered planets give versatility.
quote: It takes four or more planets to produce this result in a marked degree
locator: Alan Leo, The Art of Synthesis (How to Judge a Nativity Part II) (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1926 printing), Ch. XVI, V 'Majority Sign Positions', p.166
notes: [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.194]

rule_en: Leo's order for a detailed judgment: I Ascendant; II Ruling Planet; III Ruler's Position; IV Rising Planets; V Rising Planets in Signs; VI Individuality (Sun); VII Personality (Moon); VIII Mental Characteristics; IX the Twelve Houses.
quote: separate headings in the order in which they should be treated in making a detailed judgment of any nativity
locator: Alan Leo, How to Judge a Nativity (London: Modern Astrology Office, 1928 printing; 'Preface to the Third Edition'), Ch. XXII 'A Simple Way of Reading Horoscopes', 'Scheme for the Delineation of a Nativity', p.299
notes: Heading list taken from the book's detailed contents (p.xv) and the section headings on pp.299-326 (OCR damaged in the contents). [verify: OCR text match 1.00; found on PDF p.323]
